title: 3.	SUSPECTED OVARIAN MASSES IN PRE – MENOPAUSAL WOMEN:

blocks.content:
3.SUSPECTED OVARIAN MASSES IN PRE – MENOPAUSAL WOMEN:
⇨10% women undergo surgery due to ovarian mass.
⇨Risk of cancer
-Premenopausal – 1/1000.
-Postmenopausal – 3/1000.

Types of Adrenal Masses

1.Benign Ovarian:
1.Functional
-Follicular 3 – 5cm
-Luteal
-Theca lutein
2.Endometrioma
3.Serous cystadenoma
4.Mature Teratoma.
2.Benign Non – Ovarian.
1.Para tubal cyst
2.Hydrosalpinx
3.TO mass/abscess
4.Peritoneal pseudocyst
5.Appendiceal abscess.
6.Diverticular abscess
7.Pelvic kidney.
3.Primary Malignant Ovarian:
1.Germ cell
-Dysgerminoma
-Endometrial sinus
-Teratoma
-Choriocarcinoma
2.Sex – Cord stromal Tumors
-Estrogen secreting tumors:
⇨Granulosa – (Extreme of Age)
⇨Sertoli cell
⇨Thecoma – 1%.
-Androgen secreting:
⇨Sertoli ledying
⇨Gonad blastoma

-Non functional

Fibroma

=> Meigs syndrome

•Ascites.
•Plural effusion
•Torsion.

=> 30 year.

c. Epithelial

•Serous
▪Most common
▪10% Bilateral
•Mucinous
•Endometrial
•Clear cell
•Brener
4.Secondary – Malignant:
-Breast and GI
⇨Benign cyst with solid components:
•Fibroma
•Thecoma
•Dermoid/Teratoma
•Transitional cell
•Torsion ovary
•Cystadenoma
•Cyst adenofibroma

Assessment of ovarian masses:

⇨Risk factor for malignancy
⇨Protective factor for Malignancy
⇨Family history of CA ovary, breast. History
⇨Symptoms suggestive of

endometriosis

⇨Symptoms suggestive of

Malignancy

 

-Persistent abdominal distention
-Loss of appetite/satiety
-Abdominal/pelvic pain
- Urinary frequency/urgency.

Examination:

⇨Abdominal and vaginal examination
⇨Local lymphadenopathy
⇨Sensitivity 15 – 51% to detect ovarian mass.

Investigation:

→CA – 125 (No need in simple cyst).
⇨ CA – 125 (sensitivity 81%, specificity 75%)
-CA 125 is high in:
- Endometriosis stage III & IV => upto several hundreds.
-Fibroids.
-Pregnancy
-adenomyosis
-Pelvic infections.
-Epithelial CA – 80%.
•CA 125 is low in

Caffeine intake

TAH

Smoking.

 

⇨CA – 125:
-<200 – Further investigations to exclude common differentials.
->200 – discussion with gynae oncologists.
⇨Serial monitoring in case of raised – 125.

Tumor Makers:

-LDH
-B- HCG In complex masses
-A - FP

 

 

USG:

-Single most effective way.
-TVS preferable.
-TVS + TAS => large masses.
-TVS + Doppler + 3D imagining
⇨Improve sensitivity in complex cases.
⇨decrease no of unnecessary staging laparotomies.
-Doppler – No improvement in diagnostic accuracy.

USG rules derive from IOTA group:

→B – Rules.
→M – Rules.
→Not clearly classified.

1.B – Rules:
•Unilocular cyst.
•Presence of solid components <7mm.
•Presence of Acoustic shadowing.
•Multilocular cyst.
⇨Smooth.
⇨<10cm up to 9cm.
•No blood flow.

Sensitivity = 95%

Specificity = 91%

 

2.M – Rules:
•Irregular solid tumor
•Ascites
•Papillary structures at least 4
•Multilocular cyst
⇨Irregular
⇨> 10 cm.
•Strong blood flow.

 

Any of M – Rule

Referral to Oncological Services.

 

3.Not clearly classification:

 

•USG /Investigation by specialist in Gynecological USG.

Oncology referral:

1.Any M rule (without CT or MRI).
2.RMI of Malignancy Range.
3.CA – 125 > 200 – for further evaluation.

MRI, CT:

•Don’t improve sensitivity or specificity over TVS alone.
•Possibility of malignancy => Referral.

RMI calculation:

•Models RMI I & II.
•All women with suspected ovarian Malignancy
•To triage the management.

RMI:

•U x M x CA – 125.

U : 013

-Locularity
-Laterality
-Solid components
-Ascites
-Mets

M: 13

-Pre – M = 1
-Post M = 3.

U Scoring (013)

No: 0

1 criterion = 1 score

>1 criteria = 3 score

Management:

Ovarian Cyst

Surgical intervention

Indications

•> 7cm.
•Symptomatic of any size
•Persistent cyst
• Increasing size cyst

 

Laparoscopy: Gold std if size <7cm

 

laparotomy

- Large tumor

- Tumor with solid components

- Chemical peritonitis due to dermoid cyst 0.2% (Peritoneal lavage by cold fluids)
